title: Adoption of a Foundational Government Services Policy
text: The Snohomish County Charter Review Commission has proposed an amendment to the county charter concerning a policy to provide for, and sustain, core public services. This proposition would require the county legislature and executive branch to prioritize and protect funding for the offices of county Assessor, Auditor, Clerk, Executive, Prosecuting Attorney, Sheriff, Treasurer, and the District and Superior Court Judges. This proposition would add a new section to Article 6 of the County Charter. Should this proposition be enacted into law: Yes / No

title: Prioritize Funding of Budget Stabilization Funds
text: The Snohomish County Charter Review Commission has proposed an amendment to the county charter concerning the prioritization of the county budget stabilization funds. This proposition would require the county legislature and executive branch to prioritize the funding of the county budget stabilization funds. The purpose of these funds is to help mitigate the impacts of catastrophic economic downturns and revenue shortfalls and provide resources for emergencies and catastrophic events. This proposition would add a new section to Article 6 of the County Charter. Should this proposition be enacted into law: Yes / No

title: Converting All Elected County Offices to Non-partisan Offices
text: The Snohomish County Charter Review Commission has proposed an amendment to the county charter concerning nonpartisanship in all elected county offices. This proposition would require that all candidates for a Snohomish County elected office appear on the ballot without a political party designation and that all elected county offices be non-partisan offices. This proposition would amend Section 4.15 and Section 4.80 of the County Charter. Should this proposition be enacted into law: Yes / No

title: Increasing Public Access to County Financial Transparency
text: The Snohomish County Charter Review Commission has proposed an amendment to the county charter concerning the availability of public access to county financial information. This proposition would add a new section to Article 6 of the Snohomish County Charter. This proposition requires Snohomish County to make available, where reasonably practicable through existing systems or future modernization efforts, all financial information legally available within the county. Should this proposition be enacted into law: Yes / No

title: Requiring a 4/5 Supermajority Council Vote to Increase Taxes
text: The Snohomish County Charter Review Commission has proposed an amendment to the county charter concerning the approval of tax increases by the County Council. This proposition would require a 4/5 supermajority council vote to assess, levy, or increase any councilmanic tax. This proposition would amend Section 2.20 of the County Charter. Should this proposition be enacted into law: Yes / No

title: Amendment to Everett City Charter Sections 2.2 and 4.10
text: The amendment to Section 2.2 would require candidates for Mayor and City Council to have registered to vote in the City of Everett and resided in the City (and district if applicable) for at least one year before the deadline for filing for office; and would prohibit elected officials from holding other elected offices simultaneously. Finally, Section 4.10 would be amended to only require elected officials to take an official oath of office. Should these amendments to the Everett City Charter be enacted into law? Approved / Rejected

title: Amendment to Everett City Charter Section 3.2
text: The amendment to Section 3.2 would require the City to have at least two council meetings per month and at least 36 meetings per year; require the City to publish a schedule of those meetings every year in January and revise the procedures for determining who will preside over meetings when the Council President is absent. Should this amendment to the Everett City Charter be enacted into law? Approved / Rejected

title: Amendment to Everett City Charter Section 8.3
text: The amendment to Section 8.3 would revise the City's Civil Service rules so that the Civil Service Commission's responsibilities are consistent with the requirements of state law. Should this amendment to the Everett City Charter be enacted into law? Approved / Rejected

title: Amendment to Four Sections of the Everett City Charter
text: The amendment to Sections 11.1, 11.2, 11.3 and 11.5 would require an initiative or referendum petition be signed by qualified electors in a number equal to ten percent of the total number of votes cast at the last preceding Mayoral election; would allow for 10 days to correct faulty signatures; would streamline the initiative process; and would require the City to prepare a Fiscal Analysis of the measure that would be made available to voters. Should these amendments to the Everett City Charter be enacted into law? Approved / Rejected

title: Amendment to Eight Sections of the Everett City Charter
text: The Amendments to Sections 3.4, 3.5, 4.13, 11.6, 13.9, 15.5, 16.2, and 16.3 would modernize how the City provides the public notice by allowing the City to publish those notices, appointments, ordinances and proposed ordinances, proposed initiatives and referenda, bid advertisements, and franchise on City's website instead of requiring this information to be published in a newspaper, while also having this information available in the office of the City Clerk for examination by the public. Should these amendments to the Everett City Charter be enacted into law? Approved / Rejected

title: Capital Projects Levy for Safety and Facility Improvements

Should this proposition be approved? Yes / No

title: Concerning a Limitation on Consecutive Terms for County Council Members
text: The Clark County Charter Review Commission adopted Resolution No. 26-20 proposing an amendment to the Clark County Home Rule Charter, concerning a limitation on consecutive terms for County Council members. If approved, this amendment would limit the number of consecutive terms a County Council member could sit to three terms, with eligibility restored after one full term out of office. Should this amendment be:

If approved, this amendment would establish a new timeline for the submission of budget information, presentation, and adoption of the Clark County budget earlier than those dates set in Chapter 36.40 RCW. Should this amendment be:

title: Concerning Revised Council Powers Regarding Boards and Commissions

If approved, this amendment would give the County Council the concurrent authority with the County Manager to nominate members to all boards and commissions, with the exception of the Ethics Review Commission. Should this amendment be:

title: Concerning a Clarification of Nonpartisan Office Elections
text: The Clark County Charter Review Commission adopted Resolution No. 26-01 proposing an amendment to the Clark County Home Rule Charter, concerning a clarification of nonpartisan office elections. If approved, this amendment clarifies if two or less county candidates file for a race in the Primary, that race will bypass the Primary and proceed directly to the General Election. Nonpartisan elections for county offices shall be held in accordance with the procedures established in state law for nonpartisan elections, and shall occur in even numbered years. Should this amendment be:

title: Concerning a Required Annual Report Publication by the County Manager
text: The Clark County Charter Review Commission adopted Resolution No. 26-24 proposing an amendment to the Clark County Home Rule Charter, concerning a required annual report publication by the County Manager. If approved, the amendment would require the County Manager to present to the Council in a public meeting and publish broadly an annual statement of the County's fiscal and government affairs, and any other report which the Council may deem necessary as well as annually prepare and present to the Council in a public meeting a budget and budget message setting forth the proposals for the forthcoming fiscal year. Should this amendment be:

title: Concerning a Requirement for a Housing Impact Analysis
text: The Clark County Charter Review Commission adopted Resolution No. 26-07 proposing an amendment to the Clark County Home Rule Charter, concerning a requirement for a Housing Impact Analysis. If approved, this amendment would require prior to the adoption of any ordinance reasonably likely to have a direct and material impact upon residential housing capacity, density, permitting, subdivision requirements, parking requirements, applicable to residential development, or residential construction costs, the County shall publish a Housing Impact Analysis. Should this amendment be:

title: Concerning the Requirement of Supermajority Approval by Council for County Taxes
text: The Clark County Charter Review Commission adopted Resolution No. 26-08 proposing an amendment to the Clark County Home Rule Charter, concerning the requirement of supermajority approval by Council for County taxes. If approved, after January 1, 2027, this amendment would require any new councilmanic tax assessed, levied, or increased to have a two-third affirmative vote by the Council. Also, if approved, this amendment would not apply to fees, rates and charges, special assessments, or existing taxes levied prior to adoption of the amendment or any renewal or reauthorization of those taxes not seeking an increased tax rate. Should this amendment be:

title: Concerning the Initiative, Mini-Initiative, and Referenda Process
text: The Clark County Charter Review Commission adopted Resolution No. 26-40 proposing an amendment to the Clark County Home Rule Charter, concerning the initiative, mini-initiative, and referenda process. If approved, this amendment would reduce the number of signatures necessary for initiatives and referendums from 10% to 8%; remove calculation requirements of required signatures based on the number of votes cast within unincorporated areas of the County at the date the initiative and referendum is initiated; allow for initiatives without sufficient signatures have possible opportunity to become a mini-initiative; and permit the Auditor's Office to limited use statistical sampling techniques for signature verification. Should this amendment be:

title: Concerning Legislative Branch Performance Audits
text: The Clark County Charter Review Commission adopted Resolution No. 26-14 proposing an amendment to the Clark County Home Rule Charter, concerning legislative branch performance audits. If approved, the amendment would permit the County Council to conduct, or cause to be conducted, performance and program audits to review the effectiveness and efficiency of the programs and operations of the County. Also, if approved, this amendment would require the County Council to establish by ordinance within the legislative branch an independent county auditing process. Should this amendment be:

title: Annexation into Central Skagit Rural Partial-County Library District
text: The City Council of Sedro-Woolley adopted Resolution Number 1191-26 concerning annexation into the Central Skagit Rural Partial- County Library District. The Central Skagit Rural Partial-County Library District (Central Skagit Library) covers the surrounding rural areas within the Sedro-Woolley School District boundaries but does not include Sedro-Woolley city limits. Library service provided to Sedro- Woolley residents is based on an agreement between the City and the Central Skagit Library with fees tied to the Central Skagit Library levy rate. Voter approval of Proposition 1 will result in Sedro- Woolley becoming a part of the Central Skagit Library. Should the City of Sedro-Woolley be annexed to and become a part of the Central Skagit Rural Partial- County Library District?

title: Spokane County Fire Protection District No. 3 Emergency Medical Services Property Tax Levy
text: The Board of Fire Commissioners of Spokane County Fire Protection District No. 3 adopted Resolution #26-5 concerning a proposition to fund emergency medical services. Will Spokane County Fire Protection District No. 3 be authorized to fund emergency medical services for its citizens by imposing a regular property tax levy of $.50 or less per $1,000.00 of assessed valuation for a period of six consecutive years to be collected beginning in 2027? Spokane County Sample Ballot

place: Spokane County Fire Protection District No. 9
title: Spokane County Fire Protection District No. 9 Property Tax Levy for Fire Protection and Emergency Services
text: The Board of Fire Commissioners of Spokane County Fire Protection District No. 9 adopted Resolution No. 26-8 concerning a proposition to maintain and adequately fund District operations. This proposition authorizes the District to restore its regular property tax levy to $1.50 per $1,000.00 of assessed valuation to be levied in 2026 and allows annual levy revenue increases of up to 6% per year for the next five years (but not to exceed the $1.50 rate limit). The dollar amount of the final levy shall serve as the base for subsequent levy limitations as provided by RCW 84.55. Should this proposition be approved?

place: Spokane County Fire Protection District No. 9
title: Spokane County Fire Protection District No. 9 Fire Station and Firefighter Safety Improvements General Obligation Bonds - $70,000,000
text: The Board of Fire Commissioners of Spokane County Fire Protection District No. 9, Spokane County, Washington, adopted Resolution No. 26-9 concerning bonds to improve, construct and acquire public safety facilities. To meet increased demand for fire, emergency medical, wildfire and rescue response services, and enhance firefighter health and safety, this proposition authorizes the District to renovate, modernize and construct fire stations and facilities and replace a fire station, construct a training/classroom building, and make capital improvements; issue $70,000,000 of general obligation bonds maturing within a maximum of 20 years; and levy annual excess property taxes to repay the bonds, as provided in Resolution No. 26-9. Should this proposition be approved?

place: Spokane County Fire Protection District No. 11
title: Spokane County Fire Protection District No. 11 Emergency Medical Services Property Tax Levy
text: Shall Fire District 11 EMS levy a regular property tax in the sum of $.35 per one thousand dollars of assessed valuation each year for six years beginning in 2026

title: Authorizing the City's Salary Commission to Set the Mayor's Salary
text: Proposed Charter Amendment Proposition 2026-06 would make a salary commission responsible for setting the Mayor's salary. This amendment would change the Charter's requirements concerning the Mayor's salary. Currently, the Charter provides that the Mayor's salary should at no time be less than that of the highest paid City official or employee. This amendment would delete that requirement and instead assign responsibility for setting the Mayor's salary to the City's independent salary commission, which was established by ordinance to periodically review and fix the salaries of City Council members. Should this amendment be enacted into law?

title: Streamlining the City's Contract Review Process to Allow Electronic Signatures
text: Proposed Charter Amendment Proposition 2026-07 would streamline the contract process and allow for electronic signatures. This amendment would streamline and update the City's contract process to allow the use of electronic signatures. Currently, the Charter requires the Mayor to sign all city contracts, bonds, and instruments of any kind, and for the finance director to attest the Mayor’s signature and affix the City's seal to the document. This amendment would remove these inefficient and out-of-date requirements, authorize the Mayor's designee to sign contracts, and allow the City to use electronic signatures. Should this amendment be enacted into law?

title: Prohibition of Algorithmic Price-Fixing in the Rental Market
text: This measure would prohibit two or more landlords from entering into an agreement to establish rental prices, prohibit the use of paid algorithmic coordinating services that use systems or software to analyze public and private data about the rental market to recommend rental prices, lease renewal terms, or occupancy levels to multiple landlords, create a private right of action, establish whistleblower and anti-retaliation protections for tenants and employees, and authorize civil and criminal penalties. Should this measure be enacted into law?

title: Levy Lid Lift for Public Safety and Essential Community Services
text: The City Council of the City of Lynden adopted Resolution No. 26-1148 concerning a levy lid lift to fund public safety and essential community services. This proposition would fund public safety (police and fire), and essential community services (including park and street maintenance, restoring eliminated staff positions, reopening City Hall to the public on Fridays, and offsetting lost funding for the Lynden Community/Senior Center) by authorizing a maximum 2026 property tax levy, for collection in 2027, at $1.54304 per $1,000 of assessed value; authorizing annual increases of 3% for 2027-2035; and using the 2035 levy to calculate future levy limits. title: Regular Property Tax Levy Lid Lift
text: The Board of Commissioners of Fire Protection District 1 adopted Resolution No. 2026-07 concerning a proposition to maintain and adequately fund District operations. title: Impose a Sales and Use Tax of One-Tenth of One Percent for the Purpose of Funding Criminal Justice Services
text: The Liberty Lake City Council is calling for an election to consider the imposition of a sales and use tax of one-tenth of one percent for the purpose of funding public safety and criminal justice services pursuant to RCW 82.14.450. Should the City impose this sale and use tax?

title: Additional Sales and Use Tax for Police and Public Safety
text: The Milton City Council adopted Resolution 26-2005 concerning a proposition to maintain funding for police services and public safety. If approved, this proposition would increase the sales and use tax rate by one-tenth of one percent (0.001) to provide ongoing funding for public safety purposes permitted under RCW 82.14.450, such as providing adequate law enforcement staffing levels. This increase would become effective in 2027. Should this proposition be approved?

title: Maintaining and Expanding Local Transit Service Sales and Use Tax Increase
text: The Board of Commissioners of the Pierce County Public Transportation Benefit Area, commonly known as Pierce Transit, adopted Resolution No. 2026-006 concerning a sales and use tax for local transportation services. This proposition would authorize the collection of an additional sales and use tax of three-tenths of one percent, or three pennies for every $10 spent, to maintain and improve transit service, including adding bus routes and special event service; expanding daytime, evening, and weekend service; reducing wait times between buses; improving access to light rail, healthcare, schools, and jobs; expanding service for people with disabilities; and providing fare-free bus service to seniors and youth, effective April 1, 2027. Shall this proposition be: Approved Rejected
